newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu vows to maintain Israel budget restraint.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu vows to maintain Israel budget restraint.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, facing concerns about the expected appointed of Ariel Sharon as finance minister, said on Thursday that he would ensure the government maintained fiscal restraint.

"We are obligated to pursue complete fiscal stability. This is not related to the finance minister, this is a policy of the government and the prime minister," Netanyahu told the annual general meeting of the Manufacturers Association trade group.

He vowed to keep to the government's deficit ceiling at 2.8 percent of gross domestic product, even if it meant a further cut in spending this year, and to reduce it to 2.4 percent in 1998, as planned.
"We have determined that we need to maintain very severe fiscal restraint to achieve a budget deficit of 2.8 percent of GDP. This is not easy and another budget cut is likely," Netanyahu said.
The financial markets have expressed concern that Sharon, who is expected to be named finance minister next week as part of a cabinet shake-up, will not hold the line on spending.
Netanyahu last week approved a spending cut of 500 million to 600 million shekels, but the plan has not yet been brought before the cabinet.
